_: Tonight's film on the front page. Hand-picked cult films only: one a day, in this order, round and round. id is the Archive.org upload (it must be in the poster index with a poster), why is the one line under the title. Add to the end; never let it run dry.

films.why: Shot in three weeks for $33,000 by an industrial-film director from Lawrence, Kansas. Never got a real release. Now it's yours.
The distributor forgot the copyright notice on the print. So the film that invented the modern zombie belongs to everyone.
Stoker's widow won the lawsuit and every print was ordered burned. This one got away.
Vincent Price offers five strangers $10,000 to spend a night in the house. William Castle flew a skeleton over the audience.
Bela Lugosi died two days into shooting. Ed Wood finished it with his wife's chiropractor holding a cape over his face.
A 1922 Swedish documentary about witchcraft that turns into the strangest horror film of the silent era. Banned in the US.
Corman shot it in two days on a set left over from another film. Jack Nicholson is the dental patient.
Messiah of Evil. A coastal town where everyone stares, from the writers of American Graffiti. The supermarket scene.
Vincent Price alone in a dead city, from the novel that became The Omega Man and I Am Legend. Romero saw this first.
Sixty-eight minutes, six days of shooting, and the bleakest ending in American film. The definitive poverty-row noir.
The first zombie film. Bela Lugosi, a Haitian sugar mill, and a bride who won't stay dead.
Christopher Lee and Peter Cushing on a train across Siberia with a thing that boils brains. Telly Savalas turns up as a Cossack.
Lon Chaney Jr. minds three siblings with a disease that makes them regress. The maddest story ever told, as the poster says.
Cronenberg's telepaths. You know the scene. It was a shotgun and a latex head full of leftovers.
A beatnik busboy becomes a sculptor by accident. Corman's beat-scene satire, five days, $50,000.
A surgeon keeps his fiancée's head alive in a tray while he shops for a body. She is not grateful.
Painted shadows, a sleepwalking killer, and the twist that every unreliable narrator since owes something to.
Lon Chaney did his own makeup for the Phantom and kept it secret until the unmasking. Audiences screamed in 1925.
Peter Jackson's first film, shot on weekends over four years with his friends. Aliens harvesting humans for fast food.
Lobster monsters, a disintegrator ray, and a budget of $14,000. Beloved precisely because none of it works.
